clue.text: Girl takes turn in charge of star group

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a turn on stage is an act

explanation.surface: A young woman performs a routine while running a pop group of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belonging to a galaxy, the huge cluster of stars, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Flying squad?

parts.note: reads as the police Flying Squad, but means a team of people who fly a plane

explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Squad is a branch of London's Metropolitan Police; the question mark invites a literal reading of a squad that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The crew of an aircraft is a squad of people whose job is flying.

clue.text: Source of bitterness in a strange song, on a track that's turned up

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the following word are put in an odd order
in a down clue, turned up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rut is a track worn in the ground

explanation.surface: A bitter-sounding odd tune on a record that has surfaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' scrambles SONG to NGOS; 'turned up' reverses A RUT to TURA.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura bitters is a well-known aromatic flavouring added to cocktails to give them a bitter taste.

clue.text: Old truck's initially too dear, needing repair

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word that follows it
something needing repair must be put back together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old lorry costs far too much because it needs fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing repair' rearranges DEAR into RADE. 'Truck' is not a lorry here but the old sense of dealings, as in 'have no truck with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Truck in its old sense meant barter or commerce, the exchange of goods.

clue.text: Advent preachers confused exact reference

indicators.note: confused tells the solver to jumble the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Clergy muddled at Advent give a precise citation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a precise citation, originally pinpointing a Bible passage by its chapter and its verse.

clue.text: Support up front philosophy that's outspoken

indicators.note: up front says the support is placed ahead of the philosophy in the answer

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
Zen is a school of Buddhist philosophy

explanation.surface: A thinker defends a frank creed that he keeps right at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold and shameless speech is called this, as in a brazen lie.

clue.text: Accustomed after live music at first to be stupefied

indicators.note: after puts the word for accustomed at the end, following the other pieces

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: used, as in used to, means accustomed

explanation.surface: A person grown used to live gigs ends up dazed by them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bewildered or confused is the original meaning of this word.

clue.text: Builder reportedly has turned up, as one wishes

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top
reportedly says the word is to be heard rather than read, giving a sound like bilda

parts.note: said in a non-rhotic accent the word sounds like bilda

explanation.surface: The builder, so they say, has finally arrived, exactly when he likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns Builder into its spoken form BILDA (no R sound), and 'turned up' reverses that to ADLIB. 'has' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means at pleasure, so doing something freely and without restriction.

clue.text: Admitting right to bar passage

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: A lawyer being called to the Bar after passing an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a short passage quoted from a longer text.

clue.text: Game requiring queen in the pack

indicators.note: in puts the queen inside the word for the pack

parts.note: a pack is a bag carried on the back
R, for Regina, is the usual abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A card game that needs the queen to be in the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Brag is a British card game, an ancestor of poker.
explanation.definitionFit: This card game is a British forerunner of poker, played with a standard deck.

clue.text: One awakens as a Liberal member's about to shut up

parts.note: an arm is a member, or limb, of the body
C, for circa, is the abbreviation for about
to lock is to shut something up securely

explanation.surface: A Liberal MP is roused just as the chamber is about to close.
explanation.definitionFit: The device rings at a set hour to wake a sleeper.

clue.text: Policy outline put process in new way

indicators.note: putting something in a new way calls for the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A manager rewrites the procedure in fresh terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A document setting out the plan and terms of a share issue or a course of study.

clue.text: Time for a lark, say

definitions.meaning: British slang for a prison sentence
a lark is an example of a feathered creature

explanation.surface: Some time spent just for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing porridge is serving a jail term, in slang, while a skylark is one kind of songbird.

clue.text: Dread right ousting left from front

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, so the letter for left is removed from the front

parts.note: lawful means right, permitted by law

explanation.surface: A fear that the political right will drive the left out of the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from front' says where the L is taken away: LAWFUL loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread as an adjective means terrible or fearsome, as in a dread disease.

clue.text: They're inclined to stop getting in presents

indicators.note: getting in puts the stop inside the word for presents

parts.note: grants are gifts or presents of money
to die is to stop, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: People keen to stop being given gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Slopes are surfaces set at an angle, tilted up or down.

clue.text: Former politician's in real upset with unknown model

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: in puts the politician inside the rearranged word
upset means knocked over, so the letters are tumbled

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: An ex-MP really upset by an anonymous fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former politician' looks like one ex-MP, but the two words split: EX at the front, and MP sits inside ELAR, the scramble that 'upset' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect enough to be copied serves as an ideal pattern.

clue.text: In which sides are assumed equal, despite unknown quantities?

definitions.text: In which sides are assumed equal, despite unknown quantities?

parts.words: In which sides are assumed equal, despite unknown quantities?
parts.note: sounds like a sports match between unknown teams, but describes algebra statements whose two sides balance though they contain x and y

explanation.definitionFit: In algebra these are statements that two expressions are the same, often involving variables.

clue.text: Like some curves a doctor produced in fast cut

indicators.note: produced in places one piece inside another
cut means the word loses its end letter

parts.note: quick means fast

explanation.surface: A doctor's appointment was cut short in a hurry, like some curves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the last letter of the word for fast, leaving QUIC, and 'produced in' places A DR within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadric curve or surface is defined by a second-degree equation, such as an ellipse or parabola.

clue.text: Is welcoming new donor under one's roof

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so one piece holds the other
new suggests the letters are formed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A host makes a recent donor welcome in their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns the donor into NDOOR, and 'welcoming' wraps the clue's first word around it; 'Is' supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inside a building, sheltered rather than out in the open, is this adverb's sense.

clue.text: Against ever changing life

parts.note: V, for versus, means against

indicators.note: changing tells the solver to alter the order of the letters

explanation.surface: Opposed to life always changing.
explanation.definitionFit: Life here means vigour and liveliness, as in full of life.

clue.text: Game bordering on vice? No vice's shown up

indicators.note: bordering on asks for the edges, the first and last letters, of the word
in a down clue, shown up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a vice is a sin

explanation.surface: A dish of game close to sinful, though no wrongdoing is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'vice' give VE; 'shown up' reverses NO SIN to NISON.
explanation.definitionFit: The meat of deer is classed as game, food from hunted wild animals.

clue.text: Dress to show off about

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast or show off

explanation.surface: An outfit worn to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing or attire, especially of a distinctive kind.

clue.text: Instrument's dropped on singer

indicators.note: dropped means the word that follows is removed

parts.note: the bassoon is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: A musician's instrument fell on a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass, the lowest male voice, especially in opera.

clue.text: Bringing out what's left after girl stops administering drugs

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the girl and left go inside the other word

parts.note: doping is giving drugs, as to an athlete

indicators.note: after puts left following the girl

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An athlete's coach wonders what remains once a girl blocks the drug programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing out a photograph means treating film chemically to reveal the image.

clue.text: Machine tool recently put outside hospital

indicators.note: put outside means this word wraps around the other

parts.note: late can mean recently, as in of late
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Equipment lately moved out of the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that spins material so it can be shaped with cutting tools.

clue.text: Star actor I played with, like Olivier?

definitions.note: Laurence Olivier was made a life peer, Lord Olivier

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are put through their paces in a new order

explanation.surface: A star actor reminisces about playing alongside Olivier.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Olivier, the great English actor, became Baron Olivier; the question mark marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the realm is a member of the nobility, as the actor became.

clue.text: Part of church involved in, perhaps, ecumenism

indicators.note: involved in says the letters are contained in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some church buildings may play a role in the ecumenical movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The rounded recess at the east end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: This clue is such a burden

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden

explanation.surface: This clue weighs heavily on the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes itself: it appears under the horizontal heading of the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue sits among the horizontal entries of the grid.

clue.text: All Spain's extremely on edge at the start

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
very means extremely

indicators.note: at the start asks for the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: The whole of Spain is very nervous from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Every person, the whole lot, without exception.
